At the Races: Regional realignment

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1918 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fresh England is the ancestral home of moderate Republicans, from the Saltonstalls to the Bushes, whose fiscal conservatism and social moderation defined the national GOP for decades.
  • Last week, Yankee Republicans suffered a near-total wipeout.
  • One Republican operative sees a path out of the wilderness in a post-Trump era.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh England is the ancestral home of moderate Republicans, from the Saltonstalls to the Bushes, whose fiscal conservatism and social moderation defined the national GOP for decades.

Last week, Yankee Republicans suffered a near-total wipeout. Maine’s Susan Collins, New England's last GOP senator, lost her seat to Democrat Troy Jackson, leaving former Maine Gov. Paul LePage, who just won a House seat, as the lone Republican headed to Congress from the region. (The picture was a bit brighter at the state level, where GOP Govs. Phil Scott of Vermont and Kelly Ayotte of New Hampshire were both reelected.).

One Republican operative sees a path out of the wilderness in a post-Trump era. In an opinion piece in The Boston Globe, consultant Kristin Tate urged New England Republicans to focus on fiscal discipline and recognize that “independence from national party leadership can be a political asset, not an act of betrayal.”.

After all, as the midterm election results remind us, no political realignment lasts forever.

Three decades ago, there were plenty of moderate Democrats from Southern states serving in Congress, governor’s mansions and even the White House. But in the years since Bill Clinton's exit from the political stage, Democrats have largely written off the South.

Recent findings suggest that which is partly why last week’s Democratic wins in the Carolinas, Georgia and, perhaps most notably, Mississippi were so stunning. All the elements that powered the party to victory nationally – disillusionment with Donald Trump, a rise in economic populism and hunger for change – played a role in the South as well.

But other factors were unique to a region that has seen renewed attempts to dilute Black political power with the redrawing of House districts to favor the GOP.

The Republican redistricting gambit in Southern states did not fully yield the desired results and seems to have helped galvanize Black voters and their allies, powering Democrats to unlikely victories.

It’s too soon to say whether the GOP’s reduced hold on the South represents a temporary blip or an enduring shift.

But Joe Trippi, a longtime Democratic strategist who advised candidates in Alabama and Florida this year, has a message for his party: “We need to invest in the South.”.

According to recent reports, #MSSEN: Democrat Scott Colom defeated GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction and the first in his party to win a Senate seat in the Magnolia State since 1982.

Recent findings suggest that tar Heel tidal wave: Democrats in North Carolina have picked up at least five House seats, a striking development given the steep structural disadvantages the party faced. Prior to last week, no House Republican incumbent had lost a general election in the state since Republicans won control of the redistricting process more than a decade ago. And the Democratic gains could grow: In the 5th District, former journalist Chuck Hubbard narrowly leads 11-term Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx, and in the 3rd District, former state Rep. Raymond Smith holds a razor-thin edge over Republican Rep. Greg Murphy. The Associated Press had not called either race at publication time, though Murphy has conceded.

Republicans pick campaign chairs: Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno and Georgia Rep. Brian Jack will be the chairs of Republicans’ respective campaign committees for the 2028 cycle. GOP lawmakers held their leadership elections Tuesday, as our colleagues Savannah Behrmann and John T. Bennett reported. Senate Republicans are sticking with South Dakota’s John Thune to lead them in the next Congress, while House Republicans picked former Freedom Caucus Chair Jim Jordan as their leader.

Sources indicate that redistricting doubts: Maryland could be getting a new congressional map after voters approved a constitutional amendment that would clear the way for new lines in 2028. Our colleague Victor Feldman has more on the result and other election-related ballot measures across the country. But it’s not clear how many other states may look to redistrict next cycle after Republican efforts over the past 18 months largely didn’t pay off in last week’s elections.

Recent findings suggest that run the table: With Rep. Darren Soto winning a sixth term in Florida, no Democratic incumbent lost reelection to a Republican this year. Soto’s win in a redrawn district also meant that Florida Democrats defended all four seats the GOP had targeted under a latest congressional map.

California contest: Rep. Ken Calvert defeated fellow Republican Rep. Young Kim in a rare member-versus-member contest for a redrawn Southern California seat that turned acrimonious. Republicans are poised to hold just four House seats in the Golden State after Democrats made good on five pickup opportunities under a new congressional map.

Cheesecake Factory caucus: The latest episode of the Political Theater podcast, hosted by Roll Call editor-in-chief Jason Dick, breaks down how candidates in both parties fared in counties where The Cheesecake Factory operates, after the popular chain restaurant became something of a side character in the closing weeks of the midterm campaign.

Back to school: Newly elected members of Congress are on Capitol Hill this week for freshman orientation, an experience Massachusetts Rep.-elect Dan Koh told our colleague Nina Heller is “like high school – but it’s fun high school.” The incoming lawmakers took their class photo Thursday morning and will get to pick their Capitol Hill offices after next week’s famed lottery, Nina writes.

Tracking the count: As of 4:30 p.m. Eastern time Thursday, House Democrats had flipped 44 seats, while Republicans had picked up three. Twelve races remain uncalled, including a pair in Louisiana that will be decided by December runoffs. On the Senate side, Democrats have flipped eight seats, with only Alaska’s race still undecided.

Guv patch: Democrats flipped at least five governorships last week and will hold a majority of governor’s mansions next year. Two gubernatorial races remain uncalled by the AP: Kansas, where Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher is narrowly ahead of Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson, and Alaska, where Democratic former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is just below the 50 percent threshold to win the election outright. In territorial elections, Republicans flipped the governor’s office in Guam while voters in the Northern Mariana Islands will pick their next governor in a Nov. 20 runoff.

According to recent reports, #TNSEN: Republican Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who was elected Tennessee governor last week, is poised to pick her Senate successor. According to the Nashville Banner, the short list includes Knox County Mayor Glenn Jacobs, a former professional wrestler, Reps. Tim Burchett and Chuck Fleischmann, and Tennessee Deputy Gov. Stuart McWhorter.

2028 on the brain: A handful of House Democrats are already considering 2028 Senate bids, according to Axios, including Kansas’ Sharice Davids, North Carolina’s Don Davis and Pennsylvania’s Chris DeLuzio.

According to recent reports, senator Morrison? Minnesota Rep. Kelly Morrison is earning buzz as a potential appointee to fill the Senate seat that Democrat Amy Klobuchar is vacating to become governor, Semafor reports. House Democrats aren’t likely to be as concerned about open seats as their Republican counterparts were in recent years, given the size of the incoming Democratic majority.

AOC’s future: Progressive activists have debuted a latest organization to encourage New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028. Meanwhile, Axios reports that Ocasio-Cortez has parted ways with the digital fundraising firm she’s worked with for several years and has brought on the same firm that Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders used during his two presidential campaigns.

It has been revealed that women lead: Shirley Emehelu is New Jersey’s new lieutenant governor after Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill picked her to succeed Dale Caldwell, who resigned in September amid sexual harassment allegations and other ethical lapses. New Jersey is now one of five states to have women in both the governor’s and lieutenant governor’s offices, along with Massachusetts, Arkansas, Iowa and Virginia. Iowa will come off the list next year after an all-male Democratic ticket swept this year’s gubernatorial race, though five other states elected women to both offices last week.

It has been revealed that congress will once again be filled with losers – i.e, fresh members who have lost previous bids for elected office. Roll Call elections analyst Nathan L. Gonzales of Inside Elections returns to his biennial tradition as he runs down the latest list of “losers.”.

Industry observers note that ducking the wave: Democrats notched significant wins in unexpected places, but one state grew redder after last week’s elections. The New York Times checks in with voters in South Dakota, where the GOP won all nine statewide elections.

Here come the MBAs: Democrats with corporate connections were among the winners in last week’s elections, countering the idea that candidates with serious business credentials have struggled within the party, The Wall Street Journal reports. The field of 19 winners with M.B.A. degrees includes Costco board member Helena Buonanno Foulkes, who won the Rhode Island governor’s race, and Paige Cognetti, a Goldman Sachs alum who flipped a House seat in Pennsylvania.

Recent findings suggest that how Ricketts did it: Nebraska Sen. Pete Ricketts’ election night success was one of the few bright spots for the GOP. Ricketts fended off a challenge from independent Dan Osborn by painting him as a Democrat, questioning his authenticity and highlighting leaked audio of his comments denigrating Trump voters, writes the Nebraska Examiner.

It has been revealed that was it necessary? California redrew its congressional map to favor Democrats in response to Texas taking a similar step to boost the GOP. But some are questioning whether the state needed to cast aside its independent redistricting commission to rejigger the lines, given the scale of Democrats’ wins. “What they were literally saying is, ‘Let’s undo democracy to protect democracy,’” Lincoln Project co-founder Mike Madrid told CalMatters. “There’s something very Orwellian about it.”.

Song of the cycle: The Newly introduced York Times reviews “Talafreako,” an unlikely viral anthem celebrating the newly elected Democratic senator from Texas.

History does rhyme: An opinion piece in The (Charleston) Post & Courier argues that the win by Democratic Sen.-elect Annie Andrews is the latest in a long line of cases in which South Carolina voters bucked the idea of party bosses picking their leaders.

The man behind the grill: The Newly introduced York Times profiles Russ Hudson, the Mississippi man in Colom’s now-legendary “Pick another protein” ad.

That was the last time Democrats won 11 House seats in North Carolina.

It has been revealed that as of Thursday afternoon, they appear on track to match that number. They’ve already won nine seats – a mark they last cleared in the 1982 midterms – and they’re narrowly ahead in two more races.

If those leads hold, Democrats' 11-member delegation would look much different than the one sworn in some 66 years ago in 1961. Tar Heel Democrats taking office in January would include four women, six Black members and one Hispanic member.

Their 11 representatives (out of 12) in the 87th Congress were all white men who consistently voted to uphold racial segregation and oppose major federal civil rights legislation.

Vote counting in Alaska is expected to conclude by Wednesday, Nov. 18, the targeted date for ranked choice tabulations in races in which no candidate took more than 50 percent of the vote. As of Thursday, Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola narrowly leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in the Senate race, though she’s below the 50 percent threshold.

Meanwhile, Democrats are gathering in Denver beginning Thursday to celebrate their historic wins and plot their next steps.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that this is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey . (See our AI policy here .).

Recent findings suggest that when astronomers first spotted the supernova now designated SN 2026ahvu, it was just one of the dozens detected every day. But scientists soon realized this one was something very special, and they’ve been hustling to study it ever since.

“I think almost everyone in the world is trying to trigger a telescope and look at this,” claims astrophysicist Sumit Sarbadhicary of Johns Hopkins University.

Recent findings suggest that soon after scientists spotted the explosion on November 2, they determined it hadn’t yet peaked in brightness, giving scientists an early glimpse at the event. Even more thrilling, within a day of the explosion’s discovery, astronomers had classified it as a type Ia supernova. These particular outbursts are rare, but they’re astronomical superstars: Scientists use their trademark explosion pattern as a “standard candle” to measure distance into the universe — most notably to discover that the universe’s expansion is accelerating. And to round out a trifecta of reasons to be excited, these blasts rarely occur so close to Earth.

It has been revealed that astronomers know type 1a supernovas occur upon the reignition and resulting self-destruction of a white dwarf star, the small cool remnants of a star like the sun that’s too small to become a superdense neutron star or black hole at its demise. Scientists also know that powering back on requires reaching about 1.44 times the mass of the sun, which can occur only if something is giving the white dwarf extra mass.

According to recent reports, but scientists aren’t sure what that something is — whether these supernovas are triggered by a second white dwarf or some sort of star that’s still burning. Usually, these explosions occur so far away that astronomers can’t get a good look at where they come from. But SN 2026ahvu is perhaps 50 million light-years or less away from Earth.

“They happen so rarely at this distance that it could hopefully help us figure out why this white dwarf exploded in the first place,” states astronomer Yvette Cendes of the University of Oregon in Eugene, who has been arranging for radio telescopes to observe the outburst.

Sarbadhicary and colleagues have already submitted preliminary findings November 6 at arXiv.org suggesting that the former white dwarf was less than 100 million years old. That’s remarkably young compared with other supernovas of this type, and may help scientists finetune their understanding of these outbursts.

“These explosions have been enduring mysteries for us for decades, and whenever something happens this close, it’s just really exciting,” Sarbadhicary says.

Latest Update: Democrats mulling Iran war funding cutoff strategy

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.
  • Tim Kaine, D-Va., mentioned Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., talks with reporters in the Capitol on Sept. 30. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.

Sources indicate that sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., mentioned Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec. 11, when current funding runs out.

Industry observers note that “I know it’s going to be my main push,” he mentioned. “I have to work with colleagues to try to find some language that works. And I’m not there yet, but I’ve told everybody that’s an opportunity.”.

Democratic Sens. Michael Bennet of Colorado, Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, Tammy Duckworth of Illinois and independent Bernie Sanders of Vermont released a statement Thursday that they would oppose any deal that does not include “language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran.”.

Sources indicate that “When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war,” the senators said. “It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”.

It is unlikely that Republicans, who are in control of both chambers of Congress until January, not to mention the Oval Office beyond that, would agree to such a deal.

House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., stated earlier this week that “a Republican Congress is not going to send bills to a Republican president that he's going to veto.”.

Sources indicate that while ending the war is a top priority of Democrats as they take back power in the newly introduced Congress, insisting on doing so this year could lead to a Christmas-time partial government shutdown. If a shutdown starts after Dec. 11, it’s possible it would still be ongoing when Democrats take control of both chambers in January.

But some Democrats appeared to still be weighing how quickly to push for a cutoff of war funding.

Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash, said that whether or not Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in his job, “we’re still going to have language stopping this war.”.

She was coy on whether that fight would take place on the anticipated continuing resolution in December or wait until next year when Democrats take back power, saying that lawmakers are “looking at all options.”.

In a recent development, democrats are committed to ending the "reckless and costly war of choice in Iran," House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said Thursday. He deferred to House Appropriations ranking member Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., "to see what’s possible in advance of Dec. 11" in talks with the other top appropriators.

It has been revealed that "I don’t want to get out ahead of Congresswoman DeLauro, but House Democrats have uniformly opposed providing any additional money to Donald Trump’s war machine. to Pete Hegseth’s war machine, over in the Middle East," Jeffries remarked.

It’s not clear how long a potential continuing resolution would last, and DeLauro mentioned earlier this week that she wants it to be as short as possible.

The Office of Management and Budget has not yet submitted “anomalies” — changes to the current spending levels to be included in the continuing resolution — to Congress.

According to recent reports, the administration is considering options including a stopgap bill that would run through March, sources familiar with the talks said. But no decision on the timing covered by the anomalies has been made.

Aris Folley, Jacob Fulton and Michael Macagnone contributed to this report.

Van Hollen announces bid for majority leader, but Schumer says he has the votes

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., left, has announced a challenge to current Senate Minority Leader Charles Schumer, D-N.Y.
  • Chris Van Hollen confirmed Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen.
  • Recent findings suggest that van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., left, has announced a challenge to current Senate Minority Leader Charles Schumer, D-N.Y. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

Sources indicate that sen. Chris Van Hollen confirmed Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen. Charles E. Schumer of New York, the current Democratic leader.

Recent findings suggest that van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. He has noted since the midterm elections he was listening to fellow Senate Democrats about the possibility of a run for the top job.

“In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen noted in a statement. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need newly introduced leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”.

Schumer has already noted he has the votes needed to continue serving as the leader.

“I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the notable work ahead. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people,” Schumer stated in a statement.

Schumer's supporters were quick to highlight the success at the ballot box in 2026, with the Democratic caucus potentially growing to 56 seats if former Rep. Mary Peltola prevails in Alaska.

“Chuck has outlined an aggressive blueprint for the upcoming Democratic majority which is directly responsive to the message we heard from the voters, and he has the experience and unique mastery of the Senate process to make it happen,” Sen. Angus King, a Maine independent who caucuses with the Democrats, noted in a statement. “Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?”.

In keeping with the World Series theme, Sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., echoed King with her own statement of support for Schumer.

Sources indicate that “The Brewers just had a record season, and next year is not the time to change our management," Baldwin mentioned. "The same is true in the Senate.”.

In an interview with MS NOW about his run, Van Hollen conceded that Schumer would be the favorite in the secret-ballot contest, which will take place in December.

“Am I the underdog? Yes,” Van Hollen noted. “You’re talking about an incumbent who uses the power of incumbency to, you know, provide deals to people.”.

Industry observers note that van Hollen outlined legislative priorities including restoring Medicaid funding that Republicans cut in last year's budget reconciliation law and extending Affordable Care Act tax credits. But he suggested Democrats need to go further.

"We need to extend tax credits for the Affordable Care Act, but we can’t stop there, right? We have a completely broken health care system. It’s become profits, not people. And so my view is, we also need in the first 100 days to make health care more affordable for tens of millions of people," Van Hollen said. "We need to immediately make it clear that nobody’s going to pay one penny to subsidize data centers. ... We need to make sure that we have a livable minimum wage.".

He also mentioned he would not take sides in contested Democratic primaries, and he would make sure the DSCC did not take money from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, or AIPAC.

Van Hollen's early backers include progressive Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who emerged from a hotly contested Democratic primary in Michigan while the Senate Democratic political apparatus was backing Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich.

Sources indicate that “In April, I was the first candidate in the country to call on Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats, and I am proud to stand with him in his bid to become Senate Majority Leader,” El-Sayed said in a statement. “Michiganders demand money out of politics, money in pockets, and Medicare for All. Sen. Chris Van Hollen offers both the courage to go toe-to-toe with the Trump administration to deliver for working people and the experience to maneuver the Senate caucus. It’s why he has my full support to lead our caucus.”.

Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

MSC Cruises has launched its new year-round program from La Romana, Dominican Republic.

Departing weekly from MSC Cruises’ new year-round homeport in La Romana, the program features a variety of Southern Caribbean destinations on a seven-night sailing or an extended 14-night back-to-back itinerary.

The itineraries include Martinique, Antigua and Barbuda and the British Virgin Islands. Highlights include Fort-de-France, Martinique and Virgin Gorda’s Baths.

MSC added that each departure includes a call at Catalina Sugar Beach, where guests can enjoy the newly enhanced beach destination.

Highlights include private cabanas, beachfront dining and tropical refreshments, as well as exploring the surrounding waters on a snorkeling or catamaran excursion.

According to the press release, MSC Cruises’ Stay & Cruise options give guests more time in the Caribbean, combining their sailing with a hotel stay in the Dominican Republic before or after their cruise.

As a Lirica-class ship, the vessel combines access to exclusive destinations with a more intimate onboard experience, MSC stated, adding that a range of dining, entertainment and wellness options complements this.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ambassador Cruise Line has introduced its 2026 Black Friday campaign, offering guests complimentary drinks on selected sailings.

The offers are available on a range of adult-only cruises departing from February 2027 up to June 2028 for all fresh bookings made from 09:00 AM on November 24 through 11:59 on December 2, 2026.

The Classic Drinks Package covers house wines, selected beers and ciders, house-brand spirits, eligible house-brand cocktails and a range of soft drinks. Guests can also benefit from a 50 percent discount on premium drinks from the bar.

In addition to the Free Classic Drinks offer, the campaign also includes an upgrade to the all-inclusive Ambassador Fare from £19 per person per night.

Guests traveling alone can enjoy great deals across all four solo cabin categories as part of the promotion, while groups of 15 or more can benefit from a 5 percent discount on selected sailings, with additional complimentary places available for larger bookings.

For groups of 25 guests, Ambassador will offer one additional free place (26th place), and two free places for groups of 50 guests (51st and 52nd places).

The manufacturer mentioned in a press release that its campaign offers are available across a range of no-fly sailings onboard the Ambience and Ambition.

The sailings featured in the promotion depart between February 2027 and June 2028 to destinations including Spain, the Nordics, France, Morocco, Portugal and the Canary Islands.

The company stated that all first-time bookings on the Ambition and Ambience will benefit from the Ambassador Guarantee, which promises to reimburse any new-to-cruise guests who fail to enjoy the entertainment, cuisine and service.

The guarantee gives travelers additional confidence when booking an Ambassador cruise for the first time and applies to newly introduced-to-brand guests booking an itinerary of four nights or more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Speaking during the delivery of the MSC World Asia in Saint-Nazaire on Wednesday, Chantiers de l’Atlantique General Manager Laurent Castaing highlighted the vessel’s energy efficiency and celebrated the shipyard’s 25-year partnership with MSC Cruises.

The handover marks the 20th cruise ship built by the French yard for the company, adding a new vessel to the World Class series, which began in 2022 with the MSC World Europa.

It has been revealed that “This ship is exceptional,” Castaing said. “Following the wishes of her shipowner and thanks to our great flexibility, major new features for passengers have been added to this excellent World Class platform.”.

He also pointed to the sustainability features of the vessel, noting that its greenhouse gas emissions are 50 percent lower than the IMO reference baseline.

“What we are very proud of is the environmental performance of this ship. From a distance, she looks like others, but she is truly exceptional, and we have extensively modified the ship’s machinery,” Castaing noted.

“She is the best in energy efficiency across the entire cruise ship fleet, and by far. Few modes of transport can boast such a 50 percent reduction compared to the benchmarks. We are ahead of our competitors, and we will continue moving toward zero emissions.”.

Castaing mentioned the ship was the result of human effort, adding that thousands of people had worked on its construction since 2024.

He thanked MSC Cruises for the partnership with Chantiers de l’Atlantique, noting that the firm has now built 20 ships at the French yard over the past 25 years.

“It is exceptional. Our relationship has always been one of trust. We have not weathered any storms in our relations. Sometimes clouds have passed by, but honestly, I have never gone to Geneva with a knot in my stomach,” Castaing noted.

“Even if there were occasionally a few last-minute squabbles, our deliveries have always gone smoothly and have always been celebrated with dignity here in Saint-Nazaire, just like today, and we thank you for that,” he stated, addressing MSC Cruises Executive Chairman Pierfrancesco Vago.

Castaing remarked that MSC Cruises has brought more than 100 million hours of work to Chantiers de l’Atlantique over 25 years.

According to recent reports, “Building ships is not only about relationships between people, even though that matters enormously. There are also tens of billions of euros in orders, tens of billions of euros necessary for our trade balance,” he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, “The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” said Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., seen above. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday did little to quell bipartisan demands from Congress for an accounting of potential national security fallout from his affair with an alleged Chinese spy and talk of adding tougher chip export controls to the annual defense authorization bill.

Huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, and reports say that it was with Alice Huang, an executive at Singaporean tech tech giant and Nvidia customer Megaspeed, whom the U.S. government believes spied for China, according to recent reports. The Latest York Times and Reuters reported he also had affairs with two Nvidia employees.

Recent findings suggest that senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told reporters Thursday that he supports the Senate investigating Huang’s potential influence on U.S. artificial intelligence and chip policy.

“I think that it would make sense because of the… nature of the association… and the governments and the national security interests we were talking about here,” Thune mentioned, though he said he thought it would be “wrong” to make assumptions about how close Huang’s relationship with President Donald Trump has been.

According to recent reports, senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., echoed the need for lawmakers to delve into the scandal, saying in a post on X that “Congress must demand answers.”.

Industry observers note that “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump’s relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One?” Schumer wrote, referring to the president having invited Huang to accompany him to China in May.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said at a press conference that Reps. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., and Jim Himes, D-Conn., the ranking members of the Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees, respectively, are leading Democrats’ efforts to “get to the bottom of what has happened.”.

In a recent development, “We need a classified briefing made available to members of Congress as it relates to the Nvidia situation,” Jeffries said. “And to the extent that our national security has been compromised, the American people deserve answers, and we're going to work to make sure that happens.”.

The investigations look likely to begin before control of Congress changes hands in January.

In a recent development, rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., who chairs the House select China committee, told reporters that his panel, along with House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence, are in negotiations with Huang to find a date for his testimony before Congress.

“The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” Moolenaar said. “What ways is Chinese intelligence influencing his perspective, his perspective influencing national security policy?”.

According to recent reports, last week, the chairs of the three committees sent a letter to Huang requesting that he appear at a joint closed-door briefing. Moolenaar stated that if Huang does not agree to a date, the committees will subpoena him.

Industry observers note that late Thursday, he joined with House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., and House Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford, R-Ark., in sending a new letter to Huang seeking a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1. They also wrote to Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter seeking a similar interview on Dec. 2. Separately, Mast wrote to Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce Department undersecretary for industry and security, seeking his appearance at a committee hearing on Dec. 3.

Moolenaar also said that Congress needs to understand what privileged information Chinese intelligence may have gained access to through Huang and how they may have tried to influence U.S. policy.

Industry observers note that “We need to have strong safeguards when it comes to our technology and export controls,” Moolenaar noted. “And [Huang has] been one of the strongest proponents for not having export controls. This shines a whole fresh light on that discussion.”.

According to recent reports, also late Thursday, Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C.,  sent a letter to Huang calling on him to appear at a Dec. 3 committee hearing and another letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify at a Dec. 10 hearing "regarding recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns.".

According to recent reports, A proposed manager’s amendment to the Senate's fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill (S 4784) contains several possibilities for those safeguards, including requirements for chip security mechanisms that would allow for verification if semiconductors are diverted to countries of concern and a ban on exporting certain very powerful chips to those countries. The House NDAA does not contain similar language.

Recent findings suggest that however, House Armed Services Chair Mike D. Rogers, D-Ala., is open to the restrictions. He told reporters Wednesday that he “would like to see” semiconductor export controls in the NDAA, but that the Huang scandal had not changed his position.

Democratic Caucus Vice Chair Ted Lieu, D-Calif., told reporters on Thursday that after reports that the federal government had been aware of Huang’s affair with the alleged spy, the administration should have shared the information with Congress.

“The administration needs to be investigated for hiding this information from Congress and the American people,” he said.

Lieu also suggested that Nvidia’s reported donation to the White House ballroom project influenced the Trump administration’s decision to allow the export of some powerful Nvidia chips to China.

According to recent reports, “There is no reason to do that. That hurts our national security, and we have an opportunity right now to fix that in the upcoming National Defense Authorization,” Lieu noted.

In a recent development, mast remarked the Huang revelations could give newly introduced momentum to including chip export rules in the NDAA. He also said that his “directive” on the glitch came “straight from the admin” and informed his objectives on the committee.

“Don't let chips be smuggled to China. Make sure that American companies get to buy them first,” Mast stated. “Make sure that the machines that make them don't get sold to them, even though it's the Dutch that make the machines. Make sure that they can't access it remotely.”.

Mast’s committee has advanced many of those priorities, including some of the language included in the NDAA.

In March, the committee on a unanimous vote advanced legislation known as the Chip Security Act, which would require chip security mechanisms to verify that certain semiconductors subject to export controls aren’t diverted to countries of concern, including China and Iran.

The committee also advanced bills to require the Bureau of Industry and Security and the State Department to work with allied suppliers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment to implement export controls to prevent the equipment from going to countries of concern, and to require licenses for the export of certain powerful chips, including banning exporting certain chips to countries of concern.

Versions of all three bills are included in the Senate manager’s amendment to the NDAA.

The scandal has also led to calls for oversight of the Commerce Department, including Secretary Howard Lutnick, for its handling of export policy and actions around Huang.

In a recent development, sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., told reporters Thursday that Lutnick and Nvidia should testify “before Democrats can set the narrative.”.

In a recent development, “If there is some reasonable basis or some way to discount some of the reporting, the best way to do it is request a meeting with us and give us a briefing,” Tillis mentioned. “Because otherwise, you're going to get what you get in an oversight hearing in about six weeks.”.

Sources indicate that asked about oversight of the Commerce Department’s role in the Huang scandal, Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, who chairs the Commerce Committee, noted his panel “has engaged in vigorous oversight under Republican presidents and Democrat presidents and will continue to be [engaged in it].”.

Industry observers note that on Wednesday, prior to Huang’s resignation, Senate Banking ranking member Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller requesting that they “preserve all documents, communications, records, and other materials regarding the export of NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China.”.

“This incident raises significant concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export controls and protect our national security,” the senators wrote.

In a recent development, in a statement Thursday, Warren remarked that Huang’s resignation did not “absolve” him of the need to answer questions. She also called for the passage of stricter export controls, including the bill to ban the export of certain chips to China.

Sen. Michael Bennet, D-Colo., sent his own letter on Wednesday to Lutnick, Rubio, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, requesting an update on the Justice Department’s investigation into Megaspeed for possibly diverting U.S. chips to China.

Savannah Behrmann, John M. Donnelly, Jacob Fulton and David Jordan contributed to this report.

Industry News: Charlotte Amalie Harbor Dredging to Start This Week

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that dredging activity for the Charlotte Amalie Harbor project in St.
  • According to VIPA Executive Director Ava Penn, mobilization is underway and the dredging activity is scheduled to start by Friday, November 27, 2026.
  • The project involves dredging the harbor’s entrance channel, turning basin and West Indian Manufacturer Limited (WICO) berthing pocket in Havensight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that dredging activity for the Charlotte Amalie Harbor project in St. Thomas is set to start this week, Virgin Islands Port Authority (VIPA) shared in a press release.

According to VIPA Executive Director Ava Penn, mobilization is underway and the dredging activity is scheduled to start by Friday, November 27, 2026.

The project involves dredging the harbor’s entrance channel, turning basin and West Indian Manufacturer Limited (WICO) berthing pocket in Havensight.

Sources indicate that the multimillion-dollar maritime infrastructure investment is expected to improve navigational access to the Charlotte Amalie Harbor, accommodate the evolving needs of the cruise industry and strengthen the U.S. Virgin Islands’ position as a Caribbean cruise destination.

The dredging project will be conducted in two phases.

It has been revealed that phase 1 — Nov. 2026 through March 2027: This phase will consist of dredging the non-beach quality material from the entrance channel, turning basin and WICO berth pocket.

Phase 2 — March 2027 through October 2027: This phase will consist of dredging the beach-quality material from the entrance channel.

Dredging activities will be conducted seven days a week, Main Channel and Turning Basin from sunrise to sunset, and overnight for WICO Berthing Pocket and Bulkhead.

Preparations are underway on both St. Croix and St. Thomas, both of which welcomed the barges, dredge and survey vessels supporting the project.

At St. Croix, preparation of the temporary stockpile site, including clearing and grubbing activities, has started, with fences installed and stabilized entrances to the site constructed. Preparation of the designated quarry site will follow completion of the temporary stockpile site.

It has been revealed that on St. Thomas, a pre-dredging survey of Charlotte Amalie Harbor was conducted to establish the existing harbor conditions and assist with monitoring the dredging work.

Industry observers note that VIPA stated that its contractor cleared most of the former Addelita Cancryn Junior High School property located in Crown Bay, St. Thomas, and will use the property for dredged material storage.

Demolition of the buildings on the site started in June 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

P&O Cruises has partnered with Harding+ and Bunnahabhain to offer guests at sea the Bunnahabhain 17-Year-Old Ruby Port Cask Finish, an exclusive Islay single malt.

The drink was selected by the P&O Cruises & Harding+ teams and bottled exclusively for guests.

Limited to just over 300 bottles, the Bunnahabhain release marks a first for both P&O Cruises and Bunnahabhain, the manufacturer stated in a press release.

Recent findings suggest that the exclusive release will be available across all seven P&O Cruises ships from early November. Onboard the Iona, the launch will take place through a Bunnahabhain pop-up activation across November and December.

Carnival UK and P&O Cruises president Paul Ludlow said: “Creating memorable experiences for our guests is at the heart of everything we do and this exclusive partnership with Harding+ and Bunnahabhain is a great example of that.”.

“By working together to select and bottle a whisky available only on board our ships, we’re giving guests the opportunity to discover something genuinely unique, while bringing to life the sense of exploration and discovery that makes a holiday with P&O Cruises so special,” added Ludlow.

Lynsey Eades, head of global travel retail, CVH Spirits (Bunnahabhain Distillers), noted: “We’re incredibly excited to bring this exclusive launch to life through our partnership with Bunnahabhain and Carnival UK.”.

“This marks an exciting first at sea for Bunnahabhain and is a fantastic example of what can be achieved through strong collaboration between Bunnahabhain, Carnival UK and Harding+,” added Eades.

“Together, we’re focused on bringing distinctive brands and unique experiences to guests, and this launch reflects our shared ambition to create something truly special in the cruise retail environment. We look forward to building on this strong partnership and seeing the launch come to life.”.

According to the press release, the activation will be supported by dedicated in-store marketing materials, a whisky tasting masterclass and gifts with purchase on selected Bunnahabhain expressions, throughout the activation period.

Legislative Branch bill would hold off on GAO cuts

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A group of visitors walks past the Capitol on Sept.
  • With stopgap funding set to expire in less than a month, Senate Republican appropriators Thursday unveiled a roughly $5.3 billion draft fiscal 2027 Legislative Branch spending bill that would boost security funding and sidestep contentious debates over a key watchdog.
  • The proposal would provide $965 million for Capitol Police, a nearly $83 million hike from fiscal 2026, but still short of the more than $1 billion the department requested as threats against lawmakers rise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A group of visitors walks past the Capitol on Sept. 22. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo).

With stopgap funding set to expire in less than a month, Senate Republican appropriators Thursday unveiled a roughly $5.3 billion draft fiscal 2027 Legislative Branch spending bill that would boost security funding and sidestep contentious debates over a key watchdog.

The proposal would provide $965 million for Capitol Police, a nearly $83 million hike from fiscal 2026, but still short of the more than $1 billion the department requested as threats against lawmakers rise.

And it would bump funding for the Government Accountability Office up to $860 million, an increase of nearly 6 percent from fiscal 2026. That stands in contrast to the version of the bill advanced by the House Appropriations Committee in May, which floated slashing the GAO by 25 percent.

It joins several other draft spending bills released this week by Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, who is trying to kickstart bicameral negotiations as lawmakers stare down a Dec. 11 deadline to fund the government.

Industry observers note that her committee ran into a stalemate on topline numbers earlier this year that stopped it from marking up any of the 12 annual bills, but lawmakers nipped the threat of a government shutdown in the bud ahead of the midterm elections by pushing through a continuing resolution. With that funding now set to expire next month, appropriators are hoping they can wrap up at least some of the bills while punting the rest into the next Congress with another stopgap.

According to recent reports, the Legislative Branch bill is the smallest of the 12 appropriations bills and typically among the least controversial. But debates over the GAO have become a sticking point during the Trump administration as the agency accuses the White House of violating budget laws — a move the Office of Management and Budget has pushed back on, arguing the GAO has no authority over the administration since it is part of the legislative branch.

The GAO has been without a permanent head after its longtime leader Gene L. Dodaro retired last year, although Republicans are now making a last-ditch effort to get one confirmed during the lame-duck session before Democrats take power.

Industry observers note that the House version of the spending bill sought to bar the comptroller general from suing under the 1974 budget law restricting presidential impoundments, unless specifically authorized by Congress. But the Senate proposal includes no such language, and overall, it appears designed to avoid drastic or contentious moves.

It would also leave in place a provision that would block cost-of-living adjustments for members of Congress, whose pay has been frozen since 2009.

Senate Democrats, however, criticized the bill text after its release, saying it wouldn’t invest enough in the legislative branch.

“The Legislative Branch bill underfunds key work to support oversight of the Executive Branch, and it underfunds crucial efforts to keep the Capitol complex safe,” Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash., said in a statement.

It has been revealed that the Architect of the Capitol would get $762.5 million, though funding for House office buildings is not included in that total. The agency is requesting $1.6 billion as it seeks to begin large-scale renovations of the Rayburn House Office Building. The architect has repeatedly warned lawmakers that parts of the Capitol complex are in need of critical infrastructure upgrades, arguing that delaying renovations will only make them more expensive as things continue to deteriorate.

The bill’s $5.3 billion proposal represents funding for the Senate and legislative branch agencies, while excluding House-only funds, which are typically added later.

MSC Foundation’s Coral Restoration Efforts Resume at Ocean Cay

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (325 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cruiseindustrynews

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The MSC Foundation has resumed coral outplanting at Ocean Cay in The Bahamas, as ocean temperatures start to decline following a summer of marine heat stress.
  • The Foundation’s marine science team detected bleaching in fragments of one genotype of critically endangered staghorn coral (Acropora cervicornis), but, encouragingly, no visible signs of bleaching were observed in the critically endangered elkhorn coral (Acropora palmata).
  • Shade structures were installed over underwater nurseries to reduce exposure to intense sunlight and transferred some affected fragments to land-based nursery tanks at the Marine Conservation Center, where they are monitored while they recover.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The MSC Foundation has resumed coral outplanting at Ocean Cay in The Bahamas, as ocean temperatures start to decline following a summer of marine heat stress.

The Foundation’s marine science team detected bleaching in fragments of one genotype of critically endangered staghorn coral (Acropora cervicornis), but, encouragingly, no visible signs of bleaching were observed in the critically endangered elkhorn coral (Acropora palmata).

Shade structures were installed over underwater nurseries to reduce exposure to intense sunlight and transferred some affected fragments to land-based nursery tanks at the Marine Conservation Center, where they are monitored while they recover.

Sources indicate that “As water temperatures decline, we are resuming outplanting while continuing to monitor coral health. Our priority is to protect vulnerable corals and better understand how different genotypes respond to repeated heat stress,” said Emeline Bouchet, marine program manager at the MSC Foundation.

Recent findings suggest that “Every observation helps us refine our restoration methods. By tracking coral growth, recovery and survival, both in our nurseries and on surrounding reefs, we are building the scientific knowledge needed to make restoration more effective in a changing ocean.”.

According to data from the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Coral Reef Watch show, The Bahamas experienced significant accumulated marine heat stress during summer 2026, but satellite observations indicate that heat stress is easing in parts of The Bahamas since early November.

Although conditions are improving, continued monitoring remains crucial as severe marine heatwaves are forecasted in 2027.

Monitoring forms part of the Foundation’s long-term Super Coral Reefs Program, implemented at its Marine Conservation Center (MCC) on Ocean Cay.

The program focuses on identifying and propagating corals with promising stressor resistance and resilience characteristics, cultivating fragments in controlled land-based tanks and underwater nurseries, and outplanting them onto surrounding reefs.

In August, 32 nursery-grown fragments of elkhorn coral were outplanted on a reef near Browns Cay.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The government of Antigua and Barbuda rejected a project for a new beach club from Royal Caribbean, according to a report by The Caribbean National Weekly.

The publication said that the cruise line was planning to invest millions of dollars to build the new facility at Fort James.

Prime Minister Gaston Browne was quoted as saying that the project was a no-go due to the company’s request for exclusive access to the beach.

On a radio show, he noted that the government was unwilling to restrict public access to the coastline in exchange for the investment.

“They want exclusivity. And we said no, because our people must have access to the beach,” Browne said.

Further details of the project, including the nature of the restrictions Royal Caribbean had requested, were not revealed by the prime minister.

According to recent reports, fort James is described by The Caribbean National Weekly as a popular beach near the country’s capital city of St. John’s.

In a recent development, royal Caribbean first revealed aims for a beach club at Fort James in 2019, when it signed a memorandum of understanding with the government. The tech giant is presently building beach clubs in Mexico and the South Pacific.

The tech giant opened its first beach club, the Royal Beach Club Paradise Island in the Bahamas, in December 2025, followed by the Royal Beach Club Santorini in Greece in April.

Royal Caribbean faced issues earlier this year with a similar project at Costa Maya, in Mexico’s Quintana Roo state.

As reported by Cruise Industry News at the time, Mexican authorities rejected the company’s proposal to build a private destination near Mahahual.

When explaining the decision, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum noted that the project could be prejudicial to the region’s coastal ecosystems and the Mesoamerican Reef.

The cruise line planned to invest in building the private destination, which was to be called Perfect Day Mexico.

A petition asking the government to stop the project later reached over 5 million signatures on the Change.org platform.

Royal Caribbean’s 2026-27 season in Australia is now underway, with two Quantum-class ships sailing from ports in the country.

In addition to the Anthem of the Seas, which recently repositioned to Sydney, the firm’s seasonal deployment in the South Pacific also includes the Quantum of the Seas.

The 2014-built vessel arrived at its homeport in Brisbane in late October, kicking off a series of 28 sailings in the region.

Before completing its national season in mid-April 2027, the ship is scheduled to offer three- to seven-night itineraries to Australia’s East Coast, visiting destinations that include Airlie Beach and Cairns.

The Quantum of the Seas will also offer weeklong cruises to the South Pacific, calling at Nouméa in Upcoming Caledonia, as well as Port Vila and Mystery Island in Vanuatu.

“We’re excited to bring our award-winning Quantum of the Seas back to Brisbane, giving more Queensland families the unforgettable Royal Caribbean holiday experiences they know and love,” said Gavin Smith, vice president and managing director, Australia and Fresh Zealand, Royal Caribbean.

“With more short getaways and weekend departures, this season makes it easier than ever to escape, whether it’s a quick weekend away with friends or a longer adventure with the whole family,” he added.

In addition to sailings from Brisbane onboard the Quantum, Royal Caribbean will also offer 21 cruises from Sydney onboard the Anthem of the Seas this season.

The ship will offer three- to 11-night cruises to destinations in Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific through mid-April 2027.

Royal Caribbean is planning to expand its operations in the region in 2027-28, with three ships sailing from Australia.

As previously reported by Cruise Industry News, the Ovation of the Seas will join the Anthem of the Seas and the Voyager of the Seas for itineraries from Brisbane and Sydney.

Recent findings suggest that the AIDAcosma also received a latest biocide-free underwater coating. The coating reduces fouling and drag, lowering fuel consumption.

According to recent reports, the onboard IT infrastructure was also upgraded, resulting in the rebuilding of IT data centers and the updating of the network architecture. Restaurants, bars and shops were also equipped with newly introduced point-of-sale systems.

After its drydock, the AIDAcosma will first set sail on the “Pearls of the Mediterranean” cruise.

The “Andalusia & Canary Islands” itinerary will then reposition the ship to the Canaries for the winter.

Bipartisan process for picking GAO chief breaks down

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (938 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., speaks during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee business meeting on Sept.
  • Republican leaders have skipped a bipartisan deliberative process for recommending the next comptroller general to head the Government Accountability Office, as lawmakers prepare to consider a nomination for the post from President Donald Trump.
  • It has been revealed that sources said Trump is planning to nominate Eric Ueland, who right now serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., speaks during a Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee business meeting on Sept. 23. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Republican leaders have skipped a bipartisan deliberative process for recommending the next comptroller general to head the Government Accountability Office, as lawmakers prepare to consider a nomination for the post from President Donald Trump.

It has been revealed that sources said Trump is planning to nominate Eric Ueland, who right now serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget. The White House submitted ethics paperwork on Ueland — required for nominations — to the GAO, according to a source.

Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., on Thursday posted notice of a committee hearing Nov. 19 to examine more than a dozen presidential nominees for executive and judicial offices, including “a nominee to be Comptroller General.”.

Recent findings suggest that the post identifies by name all of the nominees except the candidate for comptroller general. The post has been filled by an acting comptroller general, Orice Williams Brown, since Gene L. Dodaro completed his 15-year term at the end of last year.

The move by Paul to short-circuit the convening of a legislative commission to recommend candidates infuriated top Democrats, who excoriated the chairman in a joint statement Wednesday night. A special bipartisan, bicameral legislative commission is supposed to recommend at least three candidates for comptroller general to the president, according to statute.

According to recent reports, homeland Security Committee GOP staff solicited recommendations for a comptroller general from some Democratic congressional offices Wednesday afternoon, imposing a deadline of 8 a.m. Thursday, according to Democratic aides.

The president nominates the head of the GAO, the investigative arm of Congress, with the advice and consent of the Senate.

Paul pushed back on the criticism Thursday, saying, “Democrats have known about this for months and months and months.” He mentioned the last time the special commission made recommendations for the office, when Barack Obama was president, “Democrats submitted their own list, Republicans submitted their own list. So they can complain all they want but they just need to make their list and submit it.”.

In the past, however, the special commission convened, sought applications for the position, interviewed candidates and deliberated before sending recommendations to the president.

A 1980 law states that when there is a vacancy in the comptroller general position, “there is established a commission to recommend individuals to the President for appointment to the vacant office,” and that the commission must submit at least three names.

Under the statute, the commission includes the speaker, Senate majority and minority leaders, House majority and minority leaders, chairs and ranking members of the Senate Homeland Security and House Oversight and Government Reform committees, and the Senate president pro tempore.

In 1981, for example, after the law took effect, the two congressional leaders, Speaker Thomas P. “Tip” O’Neill Jr., D-Mass., and Senate Majority Leader Howard H. Baker, R-Tenn., sent a letter to President Ronald Reagan saying the special commission had met and voted to recommend eight candidates to succeed Comptroller General Elmer Staats.

“The members of the Commission have taken their statutory responsibility seriously,” they wrote.

Reagan nominated Charles A. Bowsher, who was on the list, and he was confirmed.

After Bowsher’s term ended in 1996, the commission eventually formed, interviewed multiple candidates, and deliberated for several months. Republicans controlled both chambers, and Bill Clinton was president. The members of the commission could not reach agreement, and as a result, the Republicans on the committee submitted their list to Clinton, and the Democrats on the panel submitted theirs.

Clinton also had his own list. Clinton nominated David M. Walker, who was on all three lists, and he was confirmed by the Senate more than two years after Bowsher’s departure. Walker argued Thursday against short-circuiting the commission process.

“The position is of critical importance and the related statutory Commission process should not be circumvented," Walker noted. "Doing so would undercut the credibility of the person and the effectiveness of the GAO.”.

Industry observers note that walker resigned in March of 2008, when George W. Bush was still president. He appointed Dodaro as acting comptroller general when he left. The commission got going several months later, creating a website with application instructions and candidate questions.

Over the next two years, the commission interviewed some 20 candidates. Democrats and Republicans on the panel were unable to reach agreement, and Democrats, who had a majority on the commission, submitted their own list to Obama in 2010. Republicans followed up with their list.

“The Commission has been working in earnest on this undertaking for more than one year and has dedicated considerable time and effort to present you with highly qualified candidates for this important position,” then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., and then-Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, D-Nev., along with other Democratic leaders, wrote to Obama when they submitted the Democrats’ list.

The Democrats’ move drew a rebuke from Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, who was ranking member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee at the time.

It has been revealed that collins said in a statement she was “extremely disappointed” that Democrats “abruptly ended the selection process for the next Comptroller General without a bipartisan agreement” on the recommendations. “We have had several exceptionally qualified individuals apply to be the next leader of the GAO, and it should have been possible to come up with a consensus list.”.

Obama nominated and the Senate confirmed Dodaro, who was one of four recommendations from the Democrats.

The company remarked in a press release that the offer invites guests to explore the Peruvian Amazon, where its story started in 2007.

Founded by Francesco Galli Zugaro, Aqua Expeditions began with the aim of redefining small-ship exploration in the Peruvian Amazon. Twenty years later, the region remains at the heart of the company’s story, the company added.

“When I founded Aqua Expeditions twenty years ago, my vision was to create intimate, small-ship expeditions that would bring guests closer to the nature, wildlife and cultures of some of the world’s most remote destinations,” said Zugaro.

Other highlights include twice-daily excursions led by expert naturalist guides.

The manufacturer stated that the anniversary savings are available to all guests, with additional privileges for members of Circolo Aqua, Aqua Expeditions’ loyalty program.

Navigators and Explorers enjoy upgraded onboard benefits corresponding to the next loyalty tier for their expedition, while Legends receive a complimentary spa voucher and a private airport transfer.

The offer is valid for upcoming bookings on eligible 2027 departures, excluding Christmas and New Year sailings, and does not apply to solo travelers.

Recent findings suggest that it cannot be combined with other promotions, although Circolo Aqua benefits may be applied. Travel advisors can book eligible departures through Aqua Expeditions’ agent online booking system.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Supreme Court agreed on Friday to hear a challenge to President Donald Trump’s claims that an “invasion” at the southern border can be used to deny asylum claims by refugees.
  • The Trump administration had asked the justices to review a decision by the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the border wall is seen in 2021 stretching along the U.S.-Mexico border near Columbus, N.M. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

The Supreme Court agreed on Friday to hear a challenge to President Donald Trump’s claims that an “invasion” at the southern border can be used to deny asylum claims by refugees.

The Trump administration had asked the justices to review a decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit that held the president could not broadly deny asylum claims under federal law. The case is the latest high-profile fight over one of Trump’s signature domestic policies.

The administration argues in its petition for the justices to take the case that the president has broad authority over asylum claims, which includes shutting down the system entirely because he has decided he will not grant any.

In a recent development, “The proclamation thus lawfully suspends access to asylum, which is a purely discretionary benefit. The court of appeals’ insistence that aliens are entitled to file futile asylum applications elevates empty procedures over substance,” the petition states.

It has been revealed that trump issued the order on his first day in office, declaring an “invasion” on the southern border and using that as a reason to deny asylum claims by refugees who present themselves there. The order is still in place, preventing asylum claims at the U.S.-Mexico border while the lawsuit plays out.

In court filings asking the justices to take the case, the administration pointed to “dramatic” reductions in illegal border crossings, which freed up resources to combat human trafficking and other threats.

In Friday’s order, the justices agreed to hear arguments over the legality of Trump’s executive order as well as whether the lower-court judge could grant an order in favor of all asylum seekers rather than just the ones who brought the suit.

Immigration rights groups initially challenged the order and won a successful ruling from a federal judge in Washington. The administration later appealed to the D.C. Circuit, where it lost at a three-judge panel before it brought the case before the justices.

Sources indicate that the D.C. Circuit held that although federal law provides a president discretion in denying asylum claims, he cannot do so categorically.

Recent findings suggest that the ACLU and immigrant rights groups who brought the case defended the ruling in their own filing. The filing argues that Congress mandated the creation of the asylum system and the president “may not invent by fiat a new removal system that eviscerates the protections Congress mandated by statute.”.

Industry observers note that last term the justices ruled in favor of a separate policy dating to the first Trump administration that allowed officials to prevent asylum claims by stopping refugees from actually reaching the U.S. border.

A ruling in favor of the refugees could allow the administration to restart that policy and still deny asylum claims.

The case granted Friday is the latest high-profile immigration policy clash on the justices’ docket this term. Earlier this year the justices agreed to hear a challenge to the administration’s policy that most immigrants facing deportation should be detained without bond.

The justices will likely hear oral arguments and decide the case granted Friday before the end of the court’s term next June.

The case is Mullin v. Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services.

Celestyal CEO: Cooperation Key for Building Industry Resilience

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Celestyal CEO Chris Theophilides participated in a CEO interview during the ESG Shipping Awards International Conference in Athens.
  • The interview brought together the practical lessons of the recent Gulf crisis, the impact of European climate regulation on shipping competitiveness and the role of cruise operators in supporting the destinations they visit.
  • Theophilides reflected on the company’s experience in the Arabian Gulf, where its two ships remained for 47 days amid the disruption to navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, returning to the Mediterranean in April.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celestyal CEO Chris Theophilides participated in a CEO interview during the ESG Shipping Awards International Conference in Athens.

The interview brought together the practical lessons of the recent Gulf crisis, the impact of European climate regulation on shipping competitiveness and the role of cruise operators in supporting the destinations they visit.

Theophilides reflected on the company’s experience in the Arabian Gulf, where its two ships remained for 47 days amid the disruption to navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, returning to the Mediterranean in April.

“Resilience is not built up during a crisis. It is built through flexibility, preparedness and the confidence we establish with every stakeholder associated with our business. We live in a tumultuous world, and the only thing we can guarantee is that there will be another crisis. We need to build our resilience for what comes next,” he noted.

Discussing decarbonization, Theophilides emphasized that progress should be measured by results and not just ambition, particularly when addressing the challenge of adapting existing vessels to increasingly demanding environmental requirements.

Referring to Celestyal’s 2025 performance, he highlighted that the organization increased its operating days by 14 percent while reducing its overall CO₂ emissions by 10 percent.

He also underlined the importance of working closely with suppliers and partners to bring available solutions into real operating conditions, one example being Celestyal’s collaboration with Coral Marine Products in developing a biofuel blend that delivered a 21 percent reduction in CO₂ emissions.

Addressing the European regulatory landscape, including the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) and FuelEU Maritime, Theophilides stressed the importance of ensuring that environmental objectives go hand in hand with the competitiveness of the European shipping industry.

He cautioned that focusing exclusively on the operational aspects of regulation, without considering the broader value chain, could put Europe’s established expertise in cruise shipbuilding and its future investment opportunities at risk.

Industry observers note that “If we’re asked to embrace ESG, which we want to embrace ESG, and we look to investing on a 20, 30, 40-year horizon when it comes to cruise ships, you need clarity on the regulatory environment to go in with billion-dollar investments. You cannot have the situation of fragmented decisions impacting that investment thesis,” he mentioned.

Looking ahead, Theophilides expressed confidence in the industry’s ability to navigate future challenges, drawing on its experience in overcoming previous crises, emphasizing the importance of collective action and cooperation across the maritime community in building the resilience needed for the years ahead.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., leaves the Capitol after a vote on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Sources indicate that colorado Rep. Lauren Boebert, an outspoken conservative and Second Amendment provocateur, lost her bid for a fourth term to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired rear admiral in the Navy.

Laubacher was leading 48.8 percent to 47.9 percent, a margin of 3,441 votes, when The Associated Press called the race on Friday.

The red-hued 4th District, which spreads across eastern Colorado, was unexpectedly competitive this year, a sign of how deep into red turf Democrats were able to compete this year. Boebert had Donald Trump’s endorsement, but her relationship with the president has been strained at times after she began pressing for the release of files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Laubacher proved to be a strong fundraiser, hauling in $13.7 million as of mid-October to Boebert’s $1.2 million.

Boebert has been one of the most visible and controversial members of the House GOP conference since she won an upset primary in the 3rd District over five-term incumbent Republican Scott Tipton in 2020.

Recent findings suggest that A newcomer to electoral politics, she promptly positioned herself as a disruptor on Capitol Hill, heckling former President Joe Biden during his 2022 State of the Union address and tangling with a fellow GOP firebrand, former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene of Georgia, on the House floor.

In 2023, Boebert was embroiled in an embarrassing incident in a Denver theater that was captured on surveillance video. She subsequently embarked on an apology tour.

In a recent development, running for reelection the first time in the 3rd District, which is centered around Colorado’s rural Western Slope, Boebert barely won a closer-than-expected race against Democrat Adam Frisch in 2022. When Frisch announced he was trying again in 2024, Boebert switched to the 4th District, which had been considered far friendlier terrain for the GOP.

Sources indicate that this year, Democrats won all of Colorado’s House seats, except in the 3rd District, which is held by Rep. Jeff Hurd.

Mary Ellen McIntire contributed to this report.

#158545. Tech Report: 21 Best Places to Visit in December in the USA
